newsitem.title: USA: Heavy aluminum bookings point to strong US imports.
newsitem.headline: Heavy aluminum bookings point to strong US imports.

text.p: The continued high level of primary aluminum orders in the United States suggests that the domestic mills have to maintain a high level of ingot imports to meet their growing order backlog, industry analyst Stewart Spector said.
Apirl's seasonally adjusted booking rate averaged 68.5 million pounds per day, compared with 61.5 million in March, and 59.6 million in April 1996.
Non-cansheet bookings in April were 20 percent above those in the comparable month last year, and year-to-date they are up 24.1 percent.
The order rate this April for non-flat rolled products rose sharply from those recorded in the first quarter, and were up more than one-third from April 1996, Spector said.
Cansheet release schedules last month were flat compared with a year ago, and year-to-date they are down 2.3 percent.
The weight of cansheet shipments so far this year are down because beverage cans are now made of thinner sheet, but the surface area of sheet shipped was up in April, but flat in January to April.
